title: 2021 COVID-19 micro-business grant – Guidelines
summary: This page provides guidelines for the 2021 COVID-19 micro-business grant, detailing eligibility, funding use, and the application process.
who_can_apply: Must have an Australian Business Number (ABN) as at 1 June 2021, registered in, or primarily operating in, New South Wales.
Must have had an aggregated annual turnover of more than $30,000 and less than $75,000 for the year ended 30 June 2020.

Must have experienced a decline in turnover of 30% or more due to the Public Health Order over a minimum 2-week period within the period of restrictions (commenced 26 June 2021), compared to a baseline period.
Must have business costs for which no other government support is available.
Must not have applied for either the 2021 COVID-19 Business Grant or the JobSaver scheme.
For employing businesses, must maintain employee headcount from 13 July 2021 (if receiving payments from the Grant) or from the day immediately prior to the fortnight of required decline.
For non-employing businesses, the business receiving payments must be the primary income source (50% or more of total income) for the associated person.
Ineligible businesses include companies in liquidation or provisional liquidation, individuals who have entered bankruptcy, or businesses found to have engaged in fraud.
what_you_need: Australian Business Number (ABN) as at 1 June 2021.
Evidence of aggregated annual turnover (more than $30,000 and less than $75,000) for the year ended 30 June 2020.
Evidence of a decline in turnover of 30% or more due to the Public Health Order over a minimum 2-week period.
Utility bills and other supporting documents as required.
For employees: Declaration of maintaining employee headcount.
For non-employees: Declaration that the business is the primary income source (50% or more of total income).

faqs.a: The grant is for micro-businesses and provides funding to help with business costs impacted by the COVID-19 Public Health Order.

faqs.q: What is the required turnover for eligibility?
faqs.a: Applicants must have an aggregated annual turnover of more than $30,000 and less than $75,000 for the year ended 30 June 2020.

faqs.q: What evidence is needed to prove eligibility?
faqs.a: Evidence includes demonstrating a decline in turnover of 30% or more due to the Public Health Order over a minimum 2-week period, and submitting financial records like utility bills.
